location: PRD Product Scope vs FR-1, FR-3, FR-13 through FR-17, FR-21 through FR-38 and UX Core User Experience
trigger_condition: Phase 1 is treated as the implementation scope while requirements and UX flows depend on WiFi/BLE detection, campus gates, LMS integration, dashboards, questionnaires, certificate storage, dynamic RBAC, and rotating QR tokens assigned to later phases or absent from the Phase 1 scope.
guard_snippet: Tag every requirement and UX flow with its delivery phase; Phase 1 acceptance excludes later-phase capabilities or explicitly promotes them into Phase 1.
potential_consequence: Teams implement incompatible scopes, critical dependencies remain unavailable, and Phase 1 cannot satisfy its stated acceptance journeys.

location: PRD FR-3 and UJ-4
trigger_condition: Contact duration or distance is exactly 15 minutes or exactly 2 meters.
guard_snippet: Define inclusive boundaries explicitly, including sampling tolerance: duration >= 15 minutes and measured distance <= 2 meters, or state the intended alternatives.
potential_consequence: Equivalent contacts receive different outcomes across clients or services, producing missed exposures and inconsistent tests.

location: PRD FR-3 and UJ-1
trigger_condition: Two users share a closed space but distance is unknown, intermittently exceeds the threshold, or proximity samples contain gaps.
guard_snippet: Specify the closed-space qualification, allowable sampling gaps, aggregation window, and precedence between distance and room-based evidence.
potential_consequence: The system creates either excessive false-positive contacts or dangerous false negatives.

location: PRD UJ-4 and UX Effortless Interactions / Sporadic Proximity Alert
trigger_condition: The UX says contacts register without user intervention while the journey and FR-3 require users to confirm registration.
guard_snippet: Choose one consent model and define behavior for confirm, deny, dismiss, timeout, and conflicting responses from the two participants.
potential_consequence: Contacts may be recorded without consent or may silently disappear despite users expecting automatic protection.

location: PRD UJ-4 and FR-3
trigger_condition: Only one of the two proximity participants confirms the sporadic circle.
guard_snippet: Define whether one-sided confirmation creates an edge, creates a pending edge, or creates no edge, and specify its expiration.
potential_consequence: Graph records become asymmetric or indefinite pending records create misleading exposure paths.

location: PRD FR-1 and UJ-3
trigger_condition: A user is near multiple rooms, has overlapping scheduled classes, or the detected room differs from the schedule.
guard_snippet: Require an explicit room choice and show time, course, and location; never auto-select when multiple candidates satisfy the trigger.
potential_consequence: The user joins the wrong circle and unrelated attendees are later fenced.

location: PRD FR-1, UX Smart Proximity Check-in, and Accessibility Strategy
trigger_condition: A proximity prompt is dismissed, times out, arrives while the device is locked, or cannot be perceived because push, haptic, or background permissions are disabled.
guard_snippet: Provide an accessible in-app pending check-in queue and manual fallback with explicit expired and permission-disabled states.
potential_consequence: Legitimate contacts are omitted and users cannot recover from a missed ambient prompt.

location: PRD FR-2 and UX Professor Circle Dashboard
trigger_condition: Multiple staff members add the same participant concurrently or a participant self-joins while being manually added.
guard_snippet: Make circle membership insertion idempotent on circleId plus anonymousId and return the existing membership on duplicate requests.
potential_consequence: Capacity counts inflate, duplicate graph edges form, and later cascades or notifications run more than once.

location: UX Professor Circle Dashboard vs PRD DR-2, FR-18, and FR-19
trigger_condition: The participant list displays user names even though graph operations and ordinary interfaces are supposed to use anonymous identities.
guard_snippet: Show anonymous aliases or hash avatars by default; real names require an explicitly authorized, audited Health Center de-identification action.
potential_consequence: Faculty or administrators gain access to personally identifiable contact and health-context information.

location: PRD FR-2 and UX Professor Circle Dashboard
trigger_condition: A join or manual addition occurs when the displayed capacity is full, stale, zero, or changed concurrently.
guard_snippet: Enforce capacity atomically on the server and provide full, waitlisted, stale-capacity, and override-required UI states.
potential_consequence: Room capacity limits are exceeded or valid attendees are inconsistently rejected.

location: PRD FR-4, DR-3, NFR-7, and FR-8
trigger_condition: A contact edge reaches exactly 14 days old while an associated fence remains active for a full 14-day window.
guard_snippet: Define one authoritative timestamp, timezone, boundary inclusivity, and whether active-case evidence delays edge deletion.
potential_consequence: An edge may disappear before fence reevaluation, or personal contact data may remain beyond the promised retention period.

location: PRD FR-4 and NFR-7
trigger_condition: TTL cleanup is delayed by up to one hour while queries execute at the 14-day boundary.
guard_snippet: Exclude logically expired edges from every query immediately at expiresAt, regardless of physical deletion timing.
potential_consequence: Expired contacts can still trigger fences, analytics, or disclosures during the cleanup lag.

location: PRD FR-6 and UJ-1
trigger_condition: A user submits the symptom report twice, retries after a timeout, or submits from web and mobile concurrently.
guard_snippet: Require an idempotency key and collapse equivalent active symptom reports into one status-transition event.
potential_consequence: Duplicate cascades and notifications increase anxiety, cost, and graph workload.

location: PRD FR-6 through FR-10
trigger_condition: The graph contains cycles, self-edges, duplicate edges, or repeated paths to the same person.
guard_snippet: Traverse with a visited-node set, reject self-edges, deduplicate targets, and cap traversal to the defined temporal exposure graph.
potential_consequence: Recursive promotion can loop, exceed the one-second target, or send repeated alerts.

location: PRD FR-7 and UJ-2
trigger_condition: A probable contact is promoted through several confirmed or suspect paths at the same time.
guard_snippet: Define idempotent status transitions and retain a set of active causal paths rather than a single source.
potential_consequence: Race conditions overwrite exposure causes and later release a person while another valid path remains.

location: PRD FR-6 through FR-10
trigger_condition: A negative-test dissolution and a positive-test promotion for related users arrive concurrently or out of order.
guard_snippet: Version status events per subject, reject stale transitions, and reevaluate against the latest committed graph snapshot.
potential_consequence: A user may be incorrectly released, remain fenced, or oscillate between states.

location: PRD FR-8 and FR-9
trigger_condition: A negative test was collected before the relevant exposure, is too old, belongs to someone else, or has already been used.
guard_snippet: Validate certificate ownership, specimen time relative to exposure, test type, issuer, validity window, and one-time use before dissolving a fence.
potential_consequence: Invalid evidence can release an exposed person and permit campus entry.

location: PRD UJ-6 and FR-10
trigger_condition: A downstream person has no remaining Suspect path but does have an active Confirmed path, another independent exposure, or a manually imposed medical fence.
guard_snippet: Release only when no active fence cause of any supported type remains, and list every retained cause in the decision record.
potential_consequence: The system clears a fence despite another valid health restriction.

location: PRD FR-8
trigger_condition: A fence reaches its 14-day expiration while a later exposure occurred during the same fence.
guard_snippet: Track fence causes with independent start and expiry times; overall release occurs only after the last active cause expires.
potential_consequence: A later exposure is hidden by the earlier fence and the user is released prematurely.

location: PRD FR-11 and SC-1
trigger_condition: The success criterion allows 60 seconds for the cascade while alerts must be dispatched within 30 seconds and the cascade itself must complete within one second.
guard_snippet: Define separate clocks and endpoints for status commit, cascade completion, notification enqueue, provider acceptance, and user delivery.
potential_consequence: Performance can be reported as successful under one metric and failed under another.

location: PRD FR-11 and DR-6
trigger_condition: One or more of push, email, or SMS is unavailable, unconfigured, bounced, delayed, duplicated, or opted out.
guard_snippet: Track each channel independently, retry idempotently, provide an in-app alert inbox, and define the minimum accessible delivery success condition.
potential_consequence: Users miss urgent instructions or receive repeated sensitive alerts.

location: PRD FR-11 and FR-12 with Architecture Push Notifications
trigger_condition: Fence reason or recommended action appears in lock-screen push, email subject, or SMS preview visible to third parties.
guard_snippet: Use privacy-preserving notification text outside the authenticated app and reveal health details only after reauthentication.
potential_consequence: Sensitive medical or exposure information is disclosed to bystanders, shared-device users, or telecom providers.

location: PRD FR-13
trigger_condition: The LMS is unavailable, rejects the update, receives events out of order, or later receives a fence-release event.
guard_snippet: Define retry, reconciliation, idempotency, stale-event rejection, and explicit removal of Remote Attendance status.
potential_consequence: Students lose attendance credit or remain marked remote after their fence ends.

location: PRD FR-14
trigger_condition: A class circle has zero registered members, incomplete adoption, late joins, exempt instructors, or all known members are fenced only momentarily.
guard_snippet: Define the authoritative roster, minimum population, evaluation time, grace period, exemptions, and reversal behavior before canceling a reservation.
potential_consequence: Classes are canceled accidentally or remain scheduled despite all actual attendees being unavailable.

location: PRD FR-15 through FR-17 and UX Frictionless Campus Entry
trigger_condition: The app or gate scanner is offline even though the UX requires QR tokens to work without cellular data.
guard_snippet: Define offline signature validation, trusted key rotation, cached revocation limits, maximum offline age, and fail-open versus fail-closed policy.
potential_consequence: Valid users are blocked during outages or revoked and fenced credentials continue granting entry.

location: PRD FR-30 through FR-32 and UX Rotating QR Token
trigger_condition: A QR token is copied, photographed, replayed at another gate, or scanned repeatedly within its five-minute validity.
guard_snippet: Bind tokens to nonce, audience, gate or session context where feasible, and enforce replay detection with a defined offline fallback.
potential_consequence: One valid credential can be shared to admit unauthorized or fenced people.

location: PRD FR-32 and UX Rotating QR Token
trigger_condition: The user device and gate scanner clocks differ near token issuance or expiry.
guard_snippet: Specify authoritative time, allowed clock skew, warning threshold, regeneration behavior, and a recoverable clock-error state.
potential_consequence: Fresh tokens are rejected or expired tokens remain valid longer than intended.

location: PRD FR-15, FR-16, and UX Campus Entry
trigger_condition: Entry validation times out, returns an unknown status, receives malformed data, or cannot verify a signature.
guard_snippet: Add explicit Pending, Offline, Invalid, Expired, and System Error outcomes; do not map unknown states to Green.
potential_consequence: Gate staff either admit unsafe users or deny entry without actionable recovery guidance.

location: PRD FR-16 and UX Visual Design Foundation
trigger_condition: A user cannot distinguish Green and Red because of color-vision deficiency, low brightness, screen damage, or assistive technology.
guard_snippet: Pair color with icon, text, audible or haptic feedback, and accessible labels for every entry result.
potential_consequence: Users and gate staff misinterpret entry authorization.

location: PRD FR-17 and UX External User Registration
trigger_condition: A visitor abandons registration after account creation but before verification, biometric linking, or app handoff.
guard_snippet: Model resumable pending states with expiration and cleanup, and allow a non-biometric accessible recovery path.
potential_consequence: Orphan accounts and biometric references accumulate while visitors cannot complete or restart onboarding.

location: PRD FR-17 and UX Biometric Web-to-App Handoff
trigger_condition: A visitor has no biometric hardware, denies biometric permission, shares a device, or changes devices.
guard_snippet: Make biometrics optional local authentication and provide a secure PIN or verified-link alternative without transmitting biometric templates.
potential_consequence: Visitors are excluded or the backend unnecessarily stores highly sensitive biometric data.

location: Architecture Authentication Flow
trigger_condition: LDAP rejects credentials for a campus identity and the authentication chain automatically falls back to a local account with the same identifier.
guard_snippet: Separate LDAP and guest namespaces and fall back only when the account is explicitly classified as local, never after an LDAP credential failure.
potential_consequence: A local-account collision can bypass institutional authentication.

location: PRD FR-33 through FR-36 and Architecture Dynamic RBAC
trigger_condition: An administrator edits their own role, grants role-management permission, creates a circular role definition, or removes the last authorized administrator.
guard_snippet: Enforce privilege ceilings, separation of duties, cycle validation, protected system permissions, and a last-administrator invariant.
potential_consequence: Users can escalate privileges or permanently lock administrators out.

location: PRD FR-35 and Architecture JWT Authorization
trigger_condition: Permissions or employment status change while an already-issued JWT still contains old claims.
guard_snippet: Define short token lifetime, revocation or permission-version checks for sensitive operations, and immediate invalidation on role removal.
potential_consequence: Revoked users retain access to de-identification, certificates, gate scanning, or role administration.

location: PRD FR-19, FR-20, and Architecture Identity Vault
trigger_condition: A Health Center user requests de-identification outside an active care case, requests many identities, or repeatedly probes anonymous IDs.
guard_snippet: Require case-bound purpose, step-up authentication, least-privilege authorization, rate limits, immutable audit records, and alerts for bulk access.
potential_consequence: Authorized access is abused to reconstruct the contact graph's real identities.

location: PRD DR-2, FR-18, and Architecture Graph Privacy
trigger_condition: Salted hashes use predictable source identifiers, per-user salts are exposed, salts rotate, or the same person receives different hashes across services.
guard_snippet: Specify a keyed pseudonymization scheme, key ownership and rotation, stable scope, collision handling, and migration without placing source identifiers in the graph.
potential_consequence: Identifiers become guessable, unlinkable across required operations, or duplicated during key rotation.

location: PRD DR-4 vs Architecture Kafka Event Store and Audit
trigger_condition: A user requests complete deletion while identity mappings, graph events, notification logs, certificates, backups, or immutable audit records still reference them.
guard_snippet: Define deletion coverage, pseudonymization of legally retained audit data, backup expiry, completion deadline, and evidence returned to the requester.
potential_consequence: The promised right to deletion cannot be honored consistently and retained records can re-identify the user.

location: PRD DR-4 and FR-6 through FR-10
trigger_condition: A user requests deletion while actively fenced or while their contact edges are causal evidence for other active fences.
guard_snippet: Define the lawful and safety-preserving deletion policy for active cases, including immediate identity unlinking and bounded retention of non-identifying exposure evidence.
potential_consequence: Deletion either breaks active safety decisions or unlawfully retains identifiable health data.

location: PRD FR-21 through FR-23
trigger_condition: Dashboard filters produce very small groups, sparse buildings, rare departments, or combinations that isolate one person.
guard_snippet: Apply minimum cohort thresholds, complementary suppression, query-rate controls, and privacy review to every filter combination.
potential_consequence: Aggregated metrics reveal an individual's symptom or fence status.

location: PRD FR-22 and DR-2
trigger_condition: Building and department are joined with identity-vault or schedule data to produce hotspot visualizations.
guard_snippet: Use a separately aggregated read model with coarse spatial and organizational buckets; prohibit dashboard joins to identity mappings.
potential_consequence: Location and affiliation data can re-identify anonymous users.

location: PRD FR-24 through FR-26
trigger_condition: Questionnaire configuration changes while a user is answering, a response is submitted against an obsolete schema, or validation rules conflict.
guard_snippet: Version and atomically publish questionnaire schemas; bind each response to the displayed version and reject invalid configurations before activation.
potential_consequence: Responses become uninterpretable or users cannot complete mandatory entry screening.

location: PRD FR-24 through FR-26
trigger_condition: A runtime questionnaire includes questions that collect direct identity or unnecessary sensitive health information.
guard_snippet: Restrict configurable field types and data purposes, require privacy approval for sensitive changes, and prevent direct identifiers in anonymous responses.
potential_consequence: Administrators can accidentally bypass the anonymity model through configuration.

location: PRD FR-27 through FR-29
trigger_condition: A certificate upload is oversized, mislabeled, malformed, encrypted, contains active content, or carries sensitive metadata.
guard_snippet: Enforce size and type limits using content inspection, malware scanning, metadata stripping, quarantine, and safe rendering without executing embedded content.
potential_consequence: Uploads can exhaust storage, compromise staff devices, or leak identity and location metadata.

location: PRD FR-28 and Architecture File Storage
trigger_condition: The Kubernetes PersistentVolume is full, unavailable, restored from backup, or shared across replicas with inconsistent permissions.
guard_snippet: Define encrypted storage, quotas, atomic upload failure, replica-safe access, retention and deletion jobs, backup handling, and an unavailable-storage UI state.
potential_consequence: Certificates are lost, partially stored, exposed across tenants, or retained after deletion.

location: PRD FR-29
trigger_condition: A staff member views a certificate for a user or case outside their assigned scope.
guard_snippet: Authorize certificate access per case and purpose, require step-up authentication, prevent bulk export, and audit every view and validation.
potential_consequence: Sensitive medical documents are exposed through broad role membership.

location: PRD FR-37 and FR-38 vs UX Responsive Strategy
trigger_condition: The web interface is described both as full functional parity and as excluding proximity-based features.
guard_snippet: Define a platform capability matrix and specify manual equivalents and degraded states for each unavailable mobile capability.
potential_consequence: Non-smartphone users encounter missing workflows despite the stated parity requirement.

location: UX Feedback Patterns and Accessibility Strategy
trigger_condition: Glow, pulse, mesh motion, or haptic feedback affects users with reduced-motion preferences, vestibular sensitivity, or unsupported haptic hardware.
guard_snippet: Honor reduced-motion settings, provide static equivalents, avoid essential haptic-only feedback, and expose state text to assistive technology.
potential_consequence: Core status feedback becomes inaccessible or physically uncomfortable.

location: Architecture Kafka Events and Promotion Engine
trigger_condition: Kafka delivers duplicate, delayed, reordered, or poison status events, or a consumer restarts after processing but before committing.
guard_snippet: Use event IDs, per-entity versions, idempotent consumers, transactional outbox or inbox handling, retry limits, and a monitored dead-letter path.
potential_consequence: Statuses, notifications, LMS flags, and audit records diverge across services.

location: Architecture Caffeine L1 plus Redis L2 Caching and Entry Validation
trigger_condition: A status changes to Fenced but a gateway replica retains an Active result in local cache.
guard_snippet: Define cache invalidation on status commit, maximum stale duration below the safety threshold, and authoritative bypass for entry validation.
potential_consequence: A newly fenced person can receive a Green entry result.

location: Architecture Data Boundaries and Cross-Domain Communication
trigger_condition: The graph update succeeds but notification, LMS, dashboard, or audit processing fails, or the reverse occurs.
guard_snippet: Define the source of truth, transactional event publication, compensating actions, reconciliation jobs, and user-visible partial-completion states.
potential_consequence: Users see inconsistent status across the app, gates, LMS, and Health Center tools.

location: PRD NFR-1, NFR-2, NFR-3 and SC-1
trigger_condition: A cascade touches more than 10,000 active nodes, peak concurrency coincides with a large cascade, or traffic is outside the undefined normal-load profile.
guard_snippet: Specify overload behavior, hard traversal limits, queueing and backpressure, benchmark datasets, and degraded-service safety rules.
potential_consequence: Cascades time out, APIs breach latency targets, and exposure notifications arrive too late.

location: PRD NFR-4
trigger_condition: A health event, gate scan, or fence release occurs outside 7AM–10PM local time or across campuses with different timezones.
guard_snippet: Define which functions remain continuously available, authoritative campus timezone, and outage behavior outside the measured uptime window.
potential_consequence: Critical health and access workflows lack an availability commitment when users still need them.

location: UX Green Screen Entry vs PRD NFR-3 and Architecture Authentication Flow
trigger_condition: The promised end-to-end gate result under 200ms requires LDAP, database, cache, signature, network, scanner, and gate-actuator operations.
guard_snippet: Define whether 200ms is client-visible end-to-end or server processing time and specify a measurable offline or cached validation path.
potential_consequence: The headline UX benchmark is untestable or unattainable in real gate conditions.

location: PRD FR-30 through FR-32
trigger_condition: A user is promoted to Fenced after a five-minute QR token has already been issued.
guard_snippet: Define immediate token revocation or online status revalidation at scan time; offline acceptance must have an explicit bounded risk window.
potential_consequence: Previously issued tokens continue granting entry after a health-status change.

location: PRD FR-31
trigger_condition: An exit scan is missed, duplicated, processed as entry, or performed at a different gate while offline.
guard_snippet: Use distinct signed entry and exit actions, make scans idempotent, reconcile unordered events, and expose an Unknown Presence state.
potential_consequence: Campus occupancy records become inaccurate and may contaminate contact inference or emergency decisions.

location: PRD FR-36 and Architecture Audit
trigger_condition: A role or permission change affects authorization but the audit event fails or contains sensitive identity and health attributes.
guard_snippet: Fail closed for privileged mutations unless a minimal tamper-evident audit record commits, and prohibit health payloads from RBAC audit events.
potential_consequence: Privilege changes become untraceable or the audit system becomes a secondary privacy leak.

location: PRD FR-12 and UX Fence Notification
trigger_condition: The system cannot safely reveal the exact exposure reason because doing so would identify the reporting person or a very small circle.
guard_snippet: Define privacy-preserving reason categories and suppress person, class, room, or time details when they could enable re-identification.
potential_consequence: A supposedly anonymous fence alert reveals who reported symptoms or tested positive.
